data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 claims the distinction cannot be made within a single evaluation, but its own overturn conditions concede the possibility that error covariance structure could make the hypotheses identifiable or that structural assumptions within a single evaluation could suffice. The problem asks for evidence within a single evaluation that distinguishes genuine reliability from mere compliance; SRC_002 dismisses this as impossible yet lists exactly the kind of within-evaluation evidence that would break the indistinguishability. The coin-flip analogy overstates the case: within a single evaluation there are typically multiple items across varying difficulty and checklist coverage, not a single Bernoulli trial. An error covariance test — which SRC_002 itself admits as an overturn condition — is feasible across multiple items within one evaluation, so the core impossibility claim is not sustained.
